image_targets.codex: wall-mounted allocation sheet behind cracked laminate, handwritten column added in pencil at the right edge
image_targets.scanner_thumbnail: close view of a printed table with one column added by hand

en_US.title: Scrubber Allocation Sheet, Shift Office 3
en_US.scanner: Laminated allocation sheet, water-swollen. Confidence 88 percent. Hazard: none. Limit: pencil column not machine-readable.
en_US.terminal:
AEGIR CONTINUITY HOLDINGS / FORM SC-19 REV 4
SUBJECT: SCRUBBER MEDIA ALLOCATION, Q3
METHOD: ALLOCATION INDEXED TO SECTION THROUGHPUT.
SECTIONS BELOW INDEX: MEDIA ISSUE AT 0.7 OF STANDARD.
APPEAL ROUTE: CONTRACT CONTINUITY DESK.
NOTE: MEDIA IS A CONSUMABLE, NOT A SAFETY ITEM.
en_US.in_game_wiki:
Form SC-19 sets how much scrubber media each section of Sector 44 receives, indexed to throughput. Sections that fell below index received 0.7 of standard issue.

The last line does the work. Media reclassified as a consumable rather than a safety item moves it out of the safety budget, which is audited, and into the operating budget, which is not.

Someone in Shift Office 3 added a column in pencil down the right edge: section number, media received, and hours of usable air. The pencil column runs eleven sections. Four of them are under nine hours.

The pencil is not signed. Assessment: the printed sheet is the record, the pencil is the truth, and the room's scrubber bed is two metres away if the arithmetic needs checking.
en_US.field_note: Whoever kept that pencil column knew exactly what the form was doing and filled it in anyway, shift after shift. Check the bed before you trust either number.
en_US.external_site_article:
Recovered Deep Reach paperwork from HECTON-8 includes allocation forms indexing consumable supply to section productivity. Form SC-19 issued scrubber media at 0.7 of standard to sections below throughput index, and classified the media as a consumable rather than a safety item.

The classification is the significant detail: it moves the line out of an audited safety budget. Recovered copies of the form frequently carry unofficial handwritten annotations converting allocation into hours of breathable air.
en_US.external_site: Recovered Deep Reach paperwork from HECTON-8 includes allocation forms indexing consumable supply to section productivity. Form SC-19 issued scrubber media at 0.7 of standard to sections below throughput index, and classified the media as a consumable rather than a safety item.

image_targets.codex: pressure-rated containment rack still latched and intact, empty muster bench beside it, one boot on the deck
image_targets.scanner_thumbnail: priority tag zip-tied to a containment rack handle

en_US.title: Evacuation Load Priority Notice
en_US.scanner: Priority tag, polymer, still latched. Confidence 94 percent. Hazard: rack contents pressure-rated, seal intact. Limit: cannot read the reverse face without cutting the tie.
en_US.terminal:
ATLAS CONTINUITY OFFICE / NOTICE ELP-7
EVACUATION LOAD PRIORITY, BERTH 3
1. XO CONTINUITY SUBSTRATE, SEALED
2. PROCESS RECORDS AND CALIBRATION MEDIA
3. RATED HARDWARE, RECOVERABLE
4. PERSONNEL, AMBULATORY
BASIS: PROCESS INTEGRITY CANNOT BE RECONSTITUTED OFF-SITE.
en_US.in_game_wiki:
Notice ELP-7 is a numbered loading order for Berth 3. Personnel are line four.

The basis line is not a lie. Sealed substrate genuinely cannot be reconstituted off-site, and the office that wrote this had a defensible engineering argument for every line above four.

Berth 3 still holds the racks. They are latched, rated, and intact, which means they were never loaded either. Whatever window this notice was written for did not open.

The muster bench opposite is empty except for one boot, left upright. Assessment: the racks are salvageable and heavy, and the tonne-window will make you re-read line four.
en_US.field_note: Four. They wrote it down as four and then never came for one through three either. Take the rack if the window allows it, and read the number out loud before you decide that is fine.
en_US.external_site_article:
Deep Reach evacuation documentation recovered from HECTON-8 includes numbered loading priorities for berth assignments. Notice ELP-7 places sealed Xenon-Omega continuity substrate first and ambulatory personnel fourth, on the stated basis that process integrity cannot be reconstituted off-site.

The notice is defensible on each individual line, which is what makes the ordering possible. Berth 3 racks were recovered still latched, indicating the load was never executed.
en_US.external_site: Deep Reach evacuation documentation recovered from HECTON-8 includes numbered loading priorities for berth assignments. Notice ELP-7 places sealed Xenon-Omega continuity substrate first and ambulatory personnel fourth, on the stated basis that process integrity cannot be reconstituted off-site.

image_targets.codex: accounting terminal with a printed reconciliation strip curling out of the slot, sealed door behind it
image_targets.scanner_thumbnail: printed reconciliation strip showing a category change between two quarters

en_US.title: Sector Reconciliation Strip, Q4 2147
en_US.scanner: Printed reconciliation strip, thermal paper, legible. Confidence 79 percent. Hazard: none. Limit: reverse side blank, no counter-signature.
en_US.terminal:
KEELMARK LOSS DESK / RECONCILIATION 44-Q4
SECTOR 44 BIOMASS TOTAL: +18 PERCENT ON Q3.
BASIS: RECLASSIFICATION, UNRECOVERED PERSONNEL TO ORGANIC INVENTORY, PENDING DETERMINATION.
SECTOR STATUS: PRODUCTIVE.
ADJUSTER: M. IBARRA
en_US.in_game_wiki:
Sector 44's biomass total rose eighteen percent in the quarter the colony drowned, and the reconciliation records the sector as productive.

The mechanism is one word. Unrecovered personnel were moved to organic inventory pending determination of status. Inventory does not have to be searched for. It has to be counted, and counting it made the quarter look better than the one before.

Ibarra signed it. His other work is careful and his arithmetic is correct throughout.

The strip was printed inside a room whose door is still sealed from the corridor side. Assessment: the payroll cabinet behind that door holds worker IDs, and carrying them changes who answers a recovery call.
en_US.field_note: Eighteen percent up and the sector reads productive. If you pull one thing out of this room pull the ID cabinet, not the terminal - the terminal only knows what it was told.
en_US.external_site_article:
Keelmark Mutual reconciliation records from Sector 44 report a biomass increase of eighteen percent in the final quarter of 2147, with the sector's operating status recorded as productive.

The increase follows a reclassification of unrecovered personnel to organic inventory pending determination of status. The arithmetic in the recovered strips is internally consistent. Contemporary Tau Ceti reviews have treated the category change, rather than the totals, as the material fact.
en_US.external_site: Keelmark Mutual reconciliation records from Sector 44 report a biomass increase of eighteen percent in the final quarter of 2147, with the sector's operating status recorded as productive. The increase follows a reclassification of unrecovered personnel to organic inventory pending determination of status.

image_targets.codex: override request panel with a rejected stamp, cable growth crossing the panel edge, conductive biofilm on the jacket
image_targets.scanner_thumbnail: rejected override request form still seated in a panel slot

en_US.title: Override Request 6-114, Returned
en_US.scanner: Override request form, seated, returned unexecuted. Confidence 83 percent. Hazard: panel edge conductive, biofilm present. Limit: cannot read the appended reply without power.
en_US.terminal:
ATLAS CONTINUITY OFFICE / REQUEST 6-114: RETURNED
REQUESTED: MANUAL OVERRIDE, HABITAT PRESSURE AUTHORITY, SECTIONS 9-14
GROUNDS CITED BY REQUESTOR: LOCAL JUDGEMENT FASTER THAN GOVERNOR CYCLE
DETERMINATION: DENIED. GOVERNOR RETAINS AUTHORITY.
RATIONALE: DISTRIBUTED MANUAL AUTHORITY IS NOT AUDITABLE.
APPEAL: NOT AVAILABLE AT SITE.
en_US.in_game_wiki:
A shift engineer asked for the authority to open pressure doors by hand across six sections. Returned denied: distributed manual authority cannot be audited.

That rationale is true. Appeal was not available at site, and an appeal to anywhere else took years.

The form is still seated in the panel slot where it was returned, which means it came back after the requestor stopped collecting mail.

Cable growth now crosses the panel edge and the jacket carries conductive film. The governor kept that authority and has maintained the corridor ever since, by its own definition of maintenance. Assessment: the panel is live in a way the schematic does not describe. Do not bridge it barehanded.
en_US.field_note: Denied because it could not be audited. They audited the paperwork and lost the sections. Panel's grown over and still warm - gloves on, and cut nothing blue.
en_US.external_site_article:
Recovered Atlas Continuity Office records include denied requests for distributed manual pressure authority at HECTON-8, on the stated grounds that manual authority across sections is not auditable.

The determinations note that appeal was not available on site. Given interstellar communication delays measured in years, this concentrated pressure-door authority in the site governor for the remainder of the colony's operation.
en_US.external_site: Recovered Atlas Continuity Office records include denied requests for distributed manual pressure authority at HECTON-8, on the stated grounds that manual authority across sections is not auditable. The determinations note that appeal was not available on site.

image_targets.codex: dive board with a bonus band chart, grease-pencil tally beside it, worn locker row behind
image_targets.scanner_thumbnail: grease-pencil tally marks beside a printed depth-bonus band table

en_US.title: Depth Band Bonus Schedule
en_US.scanner: Painted board, grease-pencil annotation, partially washed. Confidence 66 percent. Hazard: none. Limit: tally marks cannot be attributed to a name.
en_US.terminal:
AEGIR CONTINUITY HOLDINGS / SCHEDULE DB-3
DEPTH BAND SUPPLEMENT, PER SHIFT
BAND A TO 400 M: BASE
BAND B TO 900 M: BASE +14 PERCENT
BAND C TO 1400 M: BASE +31 PERCENT
SUPPLEMENT IS VOLUNTARY AND ELECTED BY THE WORKER.
MEDICAL REVIEW: EVERY 90 SHIFTS.
en_US.in_game_wiki:
Schedule DB-3 pays thirty-one percent more for working to 1400 metres, and the supplement is described as voluntary and elected by the worker.

At 1400 metres the water reads 14 MPa. The word voluntary is accurate: nobody was ordered deeper, so nobody has to be accounted for going deeper.

Beside the printed bands somebody kept a grease-pencil tally of elected Band C shifts. The marks run in blocks of five and there are far more than ninety before the next review mark appears.

The locker row behind the board is worn unevenly. The three lockers nearest the dive hatch have the paint rubbed off the handles. Assessment: the tally is a better depth record than the schedule, and the deep lockers are the ones worth opening.
en_US.field_note: Voluntary. You elect it, so when your ears go it is a lifestyle choice. Count the tally blocks against the review mark and you will know why the third locker is empty.
en_US.external_site_article:
Deep Reach pay documentation from HECTON-8 includes depth band supplements rising to thirty-one percent for shifts working to 1400 metres, with the supplement recorded as voluntary and elected by the worker.

The election framing places responsibility for cumulative exposure with the individual rather than the roster. Recovered boards frequently carry unofficial tallies of elected deep shifts running well past the ninety-shift medical review interval printed alongside them.
en_US.external_site: Deep Reach pay documentation from HECTON-8 includes depth band supplements rising to thirty-one percent for shifts working to 1400 metres, with the supplement recorded as voluntary and elected by the worker. The election framing places responsibility for cumulative exposure with the individual rather than the roster.

image_targets.codex: draft statement on a screen with tracked deletions still visible, cursor block frozen mid-line
image_targets.scanner_thumbnail: screen showing a struck phrase replaced by a shorter one

en_US.title: Public Statement, Draft 6
en_US.scanner: Terminal holding an unsent draft, revision marks intact. Confidence 91 percent. Hazard: none. Limit: no send receipt in local queue.
en_US.terminal:
RECOVERY COMPLIANCE OFFICE / STATEMENT DRAFT 6 - NOT ISSUED
STRUCK: "an evacuation that could not be completed"
REPLACED: "a site transition without scheduled personnel movement"
STRUCK: "workers remaining in Sections 9 to 14"
REPLACED: "assets pending determination"
STRUCK: "warning suppressed"
REPLACED: "calibration drift"
REVIEW: LEGAL CLEARED. HOLD FOR RELAY WINDOW.
en_US.in_game_wiki:
Draft 6 of the public statement survived with its revision marks intact, so both versions of every sentence are readable side by side.

Nothing in the replacement column is false. A site transition without scheduled personnel movement describes what happened. Calibration drift is the correct engineering term for what a suppressed warning looks like in a log. Legal cleared it because it was clearable.

The draft was never issued. It sits in the queue holding for a relay window that the storm season closed.

What reached Tau Ceti four years later was Draft 9, and Draft 9 does not carry the struck column. Assessment: this terminal holds the only copy where the deletions are still visible, and that makes it evidence rather than a memo.
en_US.field_note: Six drafts to get from an evacuation that failed to a transition without scheduled movement. Pull the whole cassette. The version they sent is worthless without this one beside it.
en_US.external_site_article:
An unissued Deep Reach public statement recovered from HECTON-8 retains its revision history, preserving both the original and replacement wording for each edited passage.

The substitutions are technically defensible individually - evacuation failure recorded as a site transition without scheduled personnel movement, suppressed warnings as calibration drift. The version eventually received in Tau Ceti does not include the revision column, which is why the recovered draft is treated as material.
en_US.external_site: An unissued Deep Reach public statement recovered from HECTON-8 retains its revision history, preserving both the original and replacement wording for each edited passage.
